title: Search in a Rotated Sorted Array
statement:
You are given an array of distinct integers that was originally arranged in strictly increasing order, but has since been rotated to the right by some unknown number of positions (the number of positions could even be zero, meaning no rotation happened at all).

For instance, an increasing sequence could be cut at some pivot index and the front piece moved to the end, producing something like a sequence that climbs, drops once, and climbs again.

Given this rotated array and a target value, determine the index at which the target appears. If the target is not present anywhere in the array, report that it cannot be found.

Your solution must run in logarithmic time relative to the array's length, which rules out a simple left-to-right scan and instead calls for an adapted binary search that accounts for the single rotation break point.

examples.explanation: The original sorted array [10,20,30,40,50] was rotated right by 2. Scanning the rotated version, the value 10 sits at index 3.
The value 100 does not occur anywhere in the array, so the function reports -1 to indicate the target is absent.

constraints: All values in nums are unique.
nums is guaranteed to be a rotated version of an array that was originally sorted in strictly increasing order.
The algorithm must run in O(log n) time.
